kings2.14.p1.b1.text: In the second year of the reign of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz over Israel, Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah.

kings2.14.p1.b2.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not as his father David had done. … Nevertheless, the high places were not taken away, …

kings2.14.p1.b3.text: Yet he did not put the sons of the murderers to death, but acted according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, where the LORD commanded: “Fathers must not be put to death for their children, and children must not be put to death for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin.”

kings2.14.p1.b4.text: Amaziah struck down 10,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. He took Sela in battle and called it Joktheel, …

kings2.14.p2.b1.text: “Come, let us meet face to face,” he said.

kings2.14.p2.b2.text: “A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son in marriage.’

kings2.14.p2.b3.text: Then a wild beast in Lebanon came along and trampled the thistle.

kings2.14.p2.b4.text: You have indeed defeated Edom, and your heart has become proud. … Why should you stir up trouble so that you fall—you and Judah with you?”

kings2.14.p3.b1.text: But Amaziah would not listen, and Jehoash king of Israel advanced. …

kings2.14.p3.b2.text: And Judah was routed before Israel, and every man fled to his home.

kings2.14.p3.b3.text: … Then Jehoash went to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate—a section of four hundred cubits.

kings2.14.p3.b4.text: He took all the gold and silver and all the articles found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the royal palace, as well as some hostages. Then he returned to Samaria.

kings2.14.p4.b1.text: And Jehoash rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria … And his son Jeroboam reigned in his place.

kings2.14.p4.b2.text: Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

kings2.14.p4.b3.text: And conspirators plotted against Amaziah in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But men were sent after him to Lachish, and they killed him there.

kings2.14.p4.b4.text: Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.

kings2.14.p5.b1.text: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Amaziah son of Joash over Judah, Jeroboam son of Jehoash became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria forty-one years.

kings2.14.p5.b2.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD and did not turn away from all the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had caused Israel to commit.

kings2.14.p5.b3.text: This Jeroboam restored the boundary of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word that the LORD … had spoken through His servant Jonah son of Amittai, …

kings2.14.p6.b1.text: For the LORD saw that the affliction of the Israelites, both slave and free, was very bitter. There was no one to help Israel,

kings2.14.p6.b2.text: and since the LORD had said that He would not blot out the name of Israel from under heaven, He saved them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Jehoash.

kings2.14.p6.b3.text: And Jeroboam rested with his fathers, the kings of Israel. And his son Zechariah reigned in his place.
